mainTopic: Must an oath about the past be one that could also be sworn about the future (רב and שמואל), and why does שבועת העדות have its own section?
overview: רב and שמואל argue about a false oath about the past that could not be said about the future, such as 'so-and-so threw a stone into the sea.' שמואל exempts the person from a קרבן, and רב makes him liable. The גמרא first suggests that they follow an older argument between רבי יהודה בן בתירא and the רבנן about oaths on a מצוה. It rejects this and concludes that both follow the רבנן. They disagree only about whether the רבנן also require that an oath could work for both future and past. רב המנונא and רבא each challenge שמואל with a משנה, and each answers his own challenge: in those cases the person gets lashes, not a קרבן. אביי then explains where רב agrees, and asks why, according to רב, the תורה gave שבועת העדות its own section. The answer is that it brings a קרבן even when done on purpose. אביי and רבא then explain in different ways why one false oath never brings two קרבנות. Finally, the גמרא finds a contradiction between two statements of אביי. It answers that he retracted one, and it begins a second answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do רב and שמואל argue like an older dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes asking whether the רב–שמואל argument is really the older argument between רבי יהודה בן בתירא and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this the same argument that רבי יהודה בן בתירא and the רבנן have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wondering whether the argument between רב and שמואל about an oath on the past is really an older argument between תנאים. This line sets up the next move: quoting that older argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל exempts an oath that cannot work for both future and past, so he seems to demand that an oath work in "both directions." The גמרא is looking for a תנאים argument about the same idea of an oath working both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: they disagree
the Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא וְרַבָּנַן קָמִיפַּלְגִי?
phrases.english: Do they disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira and the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: 'They' are רב and שמואל, from the question just before about their argument over the stone-in-the-sea oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא וְרַבָּנַן קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question about the רב–שמואל dispute that started just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רב–שמואל dispute matches the older dispute of רבי יהודה בן בתירא and the רבנן.

steps.title: The משנה on oaths about a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: an oath to cancel a מצוה or to keep a מצוה does not bring a קרבן if broken. רבי יהודה בן בתירא would have said he should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone swore to cancel a מצוה and did not cancel it, he is exempt. If he swore to keep a מצוה and did not keep it, he is exempt. But by logic he should have been liable, as רבי יהודה בן בתירא says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the older argument: a משנה about oaths that involve a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are exempt from the קרבן of a שבועת ביטוי. The משנה notes that by logic the second case, swearing to keep a מצוה, could have been liable. That is the view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: to cancel (not do) a מצוה
to fulfill a מצוה
exempt (here, from bringing a קרבן)
by logic, by reasoning

phrases.english: As we learned: one swore to cancel a מצוה
and did not cancel it — he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: לְקַיֵּים אֶת הַמִּצְוָה וְלֹא קִיֵּים – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: To fulfill a מצוה and did not fulfill it — he is exempt.
Though by logic he should have been liable,
according to the words of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the older dispute mentioned in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath to cancel or to keep a מצוה brings no קרבן. רבי יהודה בן בתירא would hold a person liable for an oath to keep a מצוה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא argues: if an oath about an optional matter makes you liable, then an oath about a מצוה should surely make you liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא said: An optional matter is something he was never sworn to at הר סיני, and yet he is liable for breaking an oath about it. A מצוה is something he already was sworn to at הר סיני. Isn't it logical that he should be liable for it too?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא gives his reason with a קל וחומר, an argument from a lighter case to a stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath on an optional act (רשות) brings a קרבן, even though there was no earlier commitment to it. A מצוה already carries an oath from הר סיני, so it seems even weightier. He therefore concludes that breaking an oath to keep a מצוה should also bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: "if even…", the opening of a קל וחומר
an optional matter, neither commanded nor forbidden
already under oath from הר סיני (to keep the מצוות)
isn't it logical?

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira said:
If an optional matter,
which he is not under oath about from Mount Sinai —
he is liable for it;
a מצוה, which he is under oath about from Mount Sinai —
is it not logical that he should be liable for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא: וּמָה אִם הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא mentioned in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By קל וחומר from an optional oath, breaking an oath to keep a מצוה should bring a קרבן.

steps.title: The רבנן reject the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer: an optional matter works both ways ("not to" and "to"), but a מצוה does not, so the comparison fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No. You may say this about an oath on an optional matter, where the Torah treated a "not to" oath the same as a "to" oath. Can you say it about an oath on a מצוה, where the Torah did not treat a "not to" oath the same as a "to" oath?!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן break the קל וחומר by pointing out something the optional oath has that the מצוה oath lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an optional act, a person can swear either "I will" or "I won't," and both oaths are binding. With a מצוה, an oath "not to" do it does not take effect, since you cannot swear away a מצוה. The רבנן hold that only an oath that can work in both directions brings a קרבן, so an oath to keep a מצוה is also exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: "they said to him: No", the standard way to reject a קל וחומר
"no" like "yes"; a negative oath treated like a positive one
since, for the reason that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the רבנן are saying a מצוה is less important than an optional act. Their point is only that an oath about a מצוה cannot work in both directions, and that lack is what breaks the comparison.
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates the rule of the רבנן: an oath must work both ways (לאו והן) to bring a קרבן. The גמרא will now compare this rule to שמואל's demand that an oath work for both future and past.

phrases.english: They said to him: No;
if you said this about an oath on an optional matter —
since there He made the negative like the positive;
phrases.notes: "He" is the Torah: an oath "I won't" counts just like "I will."

phrases.english: will you say it about an oath on a מצוה —

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן לֹא עָשָׂה בָּהּ לָאו כְּהֵן?!
phrases.english: where He did not make the negative like the positive?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא; אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִּשְׁבוּעַת הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר of רבי יהודה בן בתירא from an optional oath to a מצוה oath.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An optional oath works as both "not to" and "to"; a מצוה oath does not. So the lighter case has a quality the stricter case lacks.

steps.title: Suggesting רב follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא and שמואל follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the suggested match: רב holds like רבי יהודה בן בתירא and שמואל holds like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא, and שמואל follows the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the comparison clearly. It is getting ready to test whether this match really holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן require an oath to work in both directions ("not to" and "to"), and שמואל requires an oath to work for both future and past. Both demand symmetry. רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not require symmetry, which seems to fit רב, who holds liable for the stone-in-the-sea oath.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say?
according to (the view of) רבי…

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא,
phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav, who said his view, follows Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
and Shmuel, who said his view, follows the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute just quoted (steps 2–4) to state the exact proposed match.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב matches רבי יהודה בן בתירא and שמואל matches the רבנן.

steps.title: On רבי יהודה בן בתירא's view, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the match: if רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not even require "not to" and "to," he surely does not require future and past. So both רב and שמואל agree on his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא, everyone agrees. Now, if he does not require that an oath work as both "not to" and "to," would he require that it work for both future and past?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. Following רבי יהודה בן בתירא, nobody would demand that an oath work for both future and past, so שמואל could not be following him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירא drops the requirement of working in both directions even for "not to" and "to." It makes no sense that he would add a new requirement of future and past. So on his view the stone oath brings a קרבן according to everyone, and רב and שמואל do not split along his line.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the view of
everyone agrees, nobody argues
now, if even… (a "how much more so" argument)
about the future and about the past

steps.whatToRemember: The suggested match fails. רבי יהודה בן בתירא does not require an oath to work in both directions, so on his view there is no room to require future and past. רב and שמואל both agree on his opinion.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira —
everyone agrees;
now, if he does not require negative and positive,
would he require future and past?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the match proposed in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that שמואל could hold his view if he followed רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Someone who does not require "not to" and "to" would surely not require future and past. So following רבי יהודה בן בתירא, both רב and שמואל would hold liable.

steps.title: רב and שמואל both follow the רבנן but disagree on how far they go
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about the view of the רבנן. שמואל follows the רבנן fully. רב says the רבנן only require 'not to / to,' which is written openly in the פסוק, but not 'future / past.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue, it is about the view of the רבנן. שמואל holds like the רבנן. רב says: the רבנן only refuse to make someone liable when the oath cannot work both as 'not to' and 'to,' because 'to do bad or to do good' is written openly. But future and past come only from extra words in the verses, so there the רבנן do make him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 6 showed that both רב and שמואל fit with רבי יהודה בן בתירא's view, so the גמרא now gives a new answer: they argue about what the רבנן mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the רבנן require both kinds of match: 'not to / to' and also 'future / past.' רב says the רבנן only require 'not to / to,' because the פסוק says it clearly. 'Future / past' is only learned from extra words, and רב holds the רבנן do not make that a requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of the רבנן
'No' and 'yes', meaning an oath not to do and an oath to do
'To do bad or to do good', the words of the פסוק
About the future and about the past
An extra inclusion learned from the wording of the verses

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל says a past oath must be one that could also be said about the future. רב says it does not have to be. Both can fit with the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenges, which all test שמואל's rule that a past oath must be able to work as a future oath.

phrases.english: Where they disagree – it is according to the Rabbis.
Shmuel holds like the Rabbis;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב – כִּי לָא מְחַיְּיבִי רַבָּנַן בְּלָאו וָהֵן,
phrases.english: and Rav: when the Rabbis do not make him liable regarding 'no' and 'yes,'
it is because 'to do bad or to do good' is written explicitly;
but future and past,
which come from an extra inclusion of the verses – they do make him liable.
phrases.notes: He means the רבנן do not accept that extra learning as a requirement, so a past oath counts even if it couldn't be said about the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 rejected the first match, this gives a new explanation of what רב and שמואל argue about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different place: inside the view of the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא and שמואל follows the רבנן
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow the רבנן. They argue about whether the רבנן also require 'future / past'

steps.title: Challenge from the oath 'I did not put on תפילין'
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא brings a משנה where a person is liable for a false oath 'I did not put on תפילין today,' even though 'I will not put on תפילין' could not work as an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא challenges: 'I did not eat today' or 'I did not put on תפילין today.' Someone said 'I make you swear,' and he answered 'Amen.' He is liable. 'I did not eat' makes sense, because it could also be 'I will not eat.' But 'I did not put on': can it also be 'I will not put on'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא attacks שמואל's rule with a משנה that seems to make someone liable for a past oath that could never work as a future oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By שמואל, a past oath only counts if the same oath could be said about the future. An oath 'I will not put on תפילין' is an oath to cancel a מצוה, so it would not take effect (step 2). Yet the משנה says he is liable, which seems to go against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I make you swear', said by someone putting another person under oath
Answering 'Amen' to an oath, which counts as swearing yourself
'It makes sense for...', used before pointing out the part that is hard

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna objects:
'I did not eat today'
and 'I did not put on tefillin today';
'I make you swear,' and he said 'Amen' – he is liable.
It makes sense for 'I did not eat':
it could also be 'I will not eat';
but 'I did not put on':
could it also be 'I will not put on'?!
phrases.notes: Swearing not to put on תפילין is swearing to cancel a מצוה, and such an oath doesn't take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests שמואל's view as explained in step 7 against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a past oath must be able to work as a future oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes him liable for 'I did not put on תפילין,' but the future form 'I will not put on' could never work as an oath, since it cancels a מצוה.

steps.title: The two cases bring different punishments
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers his own question: the משנה lists two separate cases. 'I did not eat' brings a קרבן, and 'I did not put on' brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked it and he answers it: the משנה is teaching each case on its own. 'I did not eat' makes him liable for a קרבן. 'I did not put on' makes him liable for lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers his own challenge by splitting the משנה into two cases with different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule about matching the future only matters for bringing a קרבן. 'I did not put on תפילין' is still a false oath, so he gets lashes for it, but he does not bring a קרבן. That fits שמואל.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He asks the question and he answers it himself
It teaches the cases separately, each with its own result
A sacrifice brought for breaking an oath
Lashes

steps.confusionAlert: 'Liable' (חייב) in the משנה does not mean the same punishment for both cases. One case means a קרבן, and the other means lashes.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ –
phrases.english: He asks it and he answers it:
it teaches the cases separately:
'I did not eat' – liable for a sacrifice,
'I did not put on' – liable for lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the משנה into separate cases (לצדדין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases in the משנה bring a קרבן
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'I did not eat' brings a קרבן. 'I did not put on' brings only lashes, so שמואל's rule holds

steps.title: Challenge from the oath that a stone pillar is gold
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the משנה about a pointless oath (a stone pillar is gold). עולא says it is pointless only if three people know the truth. If they don't, it counts as a regular false oath. But by שמואל, why should it count, if you cannot swear 'it will be gold'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenges: What is a pointless oath? He swore to change something people know, saying that a stone pillar in a certain place is made of gold. עולא said: that is when three people know it. So the reason is that it is known. If it is not known, he breaks a שבועת ביטוי. But why? It cannot be 'it will be gold'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second challenge against שמואל. Here someone is liable for a false past oath that could never be said about the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From עולא's words we learn that if few people know the truth, the oath counts as a שבועת ביטוי, which brings a קרבן. But nobody can swear that a stone pillar 'will become gold.' So by שמואל's rule, this oath should not count.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath in vain: swearing something plainly false or pointless
To change, meaning to deny, what is well known
Recognized by three people
An oath of utterance: a regular personal oath, which brings a קרבן if broken
'But why?'

phrases.english: Rava objects:
Which is an oath in vain?
He swore to change what is known to people –
and said about a stone pillar

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: that is in such-and-such place, that it is of gold.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא: וְהוּא שֶׁנִּיכָּר לִשְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: And Ulla said: That is when it is recognized by three people.
The reason is that it is recognized;

phrases.aramaic: הָא לֹא נִיכָּר – עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּעַת בִּיטּוּי.
phrases.english: but if it is not recognized – he transgresses an oath of utterance.
But why?
It cannot be as 'it will be of gold'!
phrases.notes: Nobody can swear a stone pillar will turn into gold, so by שמואל this past oath shouldn't count.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רָבָא אֵיזוֹ הִיא שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a second challenge against שמואל begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a past oath must be able to work as a future oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From עולא, a false oath about a pillar that few people recognize counts as a שבועת ביטוי, even though 'it will be gold' could never be sworn about the future.

steps.title: רבא answers his own question about the pointless oath
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question he asked in Step 10. If three people know the truth, the oath is a שבועת שוא. If they do not know it, it is a שבועת שקר, which brings lashes but not a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא both asked the question and answered it. If the truth is known, the person breaks the איסור of a pointless oath. If it is not known, he breaks the איסור of a false oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. The inference in Step 10 was that if the truth is not known, he breaks a שבועת ביטוי. רבא reads it instead as a שבועת שקר, which brings lashes, not a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 10 assumed that 'false oath' means the kind of oath that brings a קרבן. רבא explains that it only means the general איסור of lying under oath, which brings lashes. So שמואל can still hold that this oath brings no קרבן, because it cannot be turned into a future oath.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks the question and he answers it himself
Known, obvious (here: three people know the truth)
A pointless oath, such as swearing to something everyone knows is false
A false oath, a lie under oath (here: punished with lashes)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Counts as a false oath' here does NOT mean it brings a קרבן. It means the general לאו of lying under oath, which brings lashes.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raises the objection and he resolves it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבא, who asked the question in the step before.

phrases.english: If it is known, he transgresses because of an oath in vain;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִיכָּר – עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּעַת שֶׁקֶר.
phrases.english: if it is not known, he transgresses because of a false oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying which punishment is meant (lashes, not a קרבן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Counts as a false oath' means it brings a קרבן for שבועת ביטוי, which would contradict שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means lashes for a שבועת שקר, so שמואל's rule that no קרבן is brought still holds.

steps.title: אביי: even רב agrees about 'I know testimony for you'
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even רב agrees there is no שבועת ביטוי קרבן when someone swears 'I know testimony for you' and it turns out he does not. The reason is that the opposite oath, 'I do not know testimony,' belongs to a different category, שבועת העדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רב agrees about a person who tells his friend, 'I swear that I know testimony for you,' and it turns out he does not know any. He is exempt, because this oath does not belong in the same group as 'I do not know testimony for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a limit to רב's view. There is one case where even רב says no קרבן is brought for שבועת ביטוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath only fits שבועת ביטוי if its opposite form would also be a ביטוי oath. The opposite of 'I know testimony for you' is 'I do not know testimony for you.' That is a שבועת העדות, a separate category. So the positive form is not a ביטוי oath either, and even רב exempts it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (in this case)
An oath falsely denying that one knows testimony (ויקרא 5:1)
And it turned out
Exempt (here: from a קרבן)
It is not included in the category

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And Rav agrees in the case of one who says to his friend
"An oath that I know testimony for you,"
and it turned out that he did not know any for him, that he is exempt,
since it is not included in the category of
"that I do not know testimony for you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point that limits רב's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even by רב, a false 'I know testimony for you' oath brings no שבועת ביטוי קרבן, because its negative form is a שבועת העדות.

steps.title: Past-tense testimony oaths depend on the argument
steps.stepSummary: אביי continues: oaths such as 'I knew / I did not know testimony' or 'I testified / I did not testify' depend on the argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I knew' and 'I did not know': this is the argument. 'I testified' and 'I did not testify': this is the argument.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי lists cases that are not covered by what he just said. In these cases, רב and שמואל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These oaths are not a שבועת העדות, because the person is not refusing to testify. They also cannot be turned into future oaths. So רב, who does not require a future form, makes him bring a קרבן, and שמואל exempts him.

keyTerms.meaning: I knew
I testified
A disagreement (here: between רב and שמואל)

steps.whatToRemember: Only 'I know testimony for you' is exempt by everyone. Past-tense testimony oaths like 'I knew' or 'I testified' depend on the argument between רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: "I knew" and "I did not know": it is a dispute.
phrases.notes: This is the argument between רב and שמואל about oaths that cannot be turned into the future.

phrases.english: "I testified" and "I did not testify": it is a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's statement and marks where the agreement ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Past-tense oaths about testimony that are not a שבועת העדות depend on the argument between רב and שמואל.

steps.title: Why did the Torah separate the oath of testimony, according to רב?
steps.stepSummary: By שמואל, the תורה had to give שבועת העדות its own פסוק, because it cannot be turned into a future oath. By רב, every שבועת העדות would already fit under שבועת ביטוי, so why did the תורה separate it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense by שמואל, who says that something that cannot be said in the future does not make you liable in the past. That is why the תורה took שבועת העדות out of the group of שבועת ביטוי. But by רב, for what הלכה did the תורה take it out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב: his view seems to make the separate פסוק for שבועת העדות unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath of testimony is always about the present or past, so it cannot be turned into a future oath. For שמואל, that means it is not a ביטוי oath, and the תורה needed a separate פסוק to make it liable. For רב, past oaths count even without a future form, so the separate category seems to have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one view, before asking on the other)
For the future
For the past
The תורה took it out (made it a separate category)
For what הלכה? What difference does it make?

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic way to check a view: if it makes a פסוק unnecessary, that view has to explain what the פסוק is for.

phrases.english: It works well for Shmuel, who says:
a matter that does not apply in the future
one is not liable for it in the past;
for this reason the Merciful One took the oath of testimony out
from the category of an oath on an utterance.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב, לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא אַפְּקַהּ רַחֲמָנָא?
phrases.english: But according to Rav, for what halakha did the Merciful One take it out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רב's view
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a past oath brings a קרבן even if it cannot be turned into a future oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רב, שבועת העדות would already be included in שבועת ביטוי, so the separate פסוק for it seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The רבנן suggest: the separate section makes him bring two offerings
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן suggest to אביי that, according to רב, the תורה separated שבועת העדות so that a person who swears falsely would bring two קרבנות: one for שבועת ביטוי and one for שבועת העדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said in front of אביי: The תורה separated it so that he would be obligated for it twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן offer an answer to the question from Step 14: why did the תורה give שבועת העדות its own section if רב says it already counts as a שבועת ביטוי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their idea is that the separate section is not repeating anything. It adds a second obligation. One false oath would bring two קרבנות, one under each category.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (here, the students learning with אביי)
In front of him
To make him obligated (liable)
Two (here: two קרבנות)

phrases.english: The Rabbis said it in front of Abaye:
To make him liable for it twice.
phrases.notes: He means two קרבנות for the one false oath, one as a שבועת ביטוי and one as a שבועת העדות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question in Step 14 about why שבועת העדות has its own section according to רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the separate section a new job: a second, extra obligation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The separate section seemed pointless, because שבועת ביטוי already covers this oath according to רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The section is there to add a second קרבן for the same false oath.

steps.title: אביי rejects two offerings, based on a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the suggestion. A ברייתא learns from the words ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ that a person is obligated in only one קרבן, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: You cannot say two. It is taught in a ברייתא: 'For one of these' teaches that you obligate him for one, and you do not obligate him for two.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back the answer of the רבנן from Step 15. He quotes a ברייתא showing that the תורה never gives two of these קרבנות for one act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about this קרבן says 'in one of these.' The ברייתא reads this as a limit: one קרבן only. So the separate section for שבועת העדות cannot be there to add a second קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say (that)
For one of these (words of the פסוק)
You obligate him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: תַּרְתֵּי לָא מָצִיתוּ אָמְרִיתוּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: You cannot say two,
As it is taught: 'In one of these' –
For one you obligate him,
And you do not obligate him for two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of the רבנן in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that the separate section adds a second קרבן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא learns from ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ that one act never brings two קרבנות.

steps.title: So according to אביי, what is the separate section for?
steps.stepSummary: Since two קרבנות is ruled out, the גמרא asks again: according to אביי's view of רב, what law does the תורה teach by putting שבועת העדות in its own section?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, for what law did the תורה take it out on its own?
steps.whatsHappening: The question from Step 14 comes back, because the answer of the רבנן was rejected. This line sets up the גמרא's real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי removed the 'two קרבנות' answer, so now he must give a different purpose for the separate section. Otherwise the question against רב stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (What does this teach?)
He took it out (separated it)
The Merciful One (the תורה)

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, for what law did the Merciful One take it out?
phrases.notes: 'It' is שבועת העדות: why did the תורה take it out of שבועת ביטוי and give it its own section?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי rejected the answer in Step 16, the question from Step 14 is asked again, now aimed at אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view of רב, that every false שבועת העדות is already a שבועת ביטוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is already covered, and it does not add a second קרבן, the separate section seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: The answer: one who lied on purpose also brings the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. By all the other cases of this קרבן, the תורה says ״וְנֶעְלַם״ (it was hidden from him). By שבועת העדות it does not say this, which teaches that a person who lied on purpose (מזיד) brings the קרבן just like one who did it by mistake (שוגג).
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: By all of them it says 'and it was hidden,' and here it does not say 'and it was hidden.' This teaches that he is obligated for doing it on purpose just like doing it by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 17. The separate section teaches a special rule for שבועת העדות: even an on-purpose liar brings the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a קרבן is brought only for a mistake, and the other cases say ״וְנֶעְלַם״ to show this. Since that word is missing by שבועת העדות, it gets a unique rule: a קרבן even for מזיד. That is why the תורה needed a separate section for it, even according to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was hidden from him (he did not realize)
Doing something on purpose
Doing something by mistake
By all of them (the other cases of this קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רב's view stands: the separate section for שבועת העדות is not about two קרבנות. It teaches that a false שבועת העדות brings a קרבן even when done on purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: Normally a קרבן is only for a mistake (שוגג). שבועת העדות is an exception: here even the on-purpose liar (מזיד) brings it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the תורה needed a separate section for שבועת העדות even according to רב, so the question from Step 14 is answered.

phrases.english: For that which is taught: By all of them it says 'and it was hidden,'
And here it does not say 'and it was hidden';
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the section about שבועת העדות.

phrases.english: To make him liable for the intentional act like the unintentional one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a unique law that only the separate section could teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The separate section for שבועת העדות seemed to teach nothing new according to רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The section teaches that a false שבועת העדות brings a קרבן even when done on purpose, because ״וְנֶעְלַם״ is missing there.

steps.title: The רבנן suggest: one קרבן on purpose, two by mistake
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell אביי the ״לְאַחַת״ limit may apply only on purpose, so by mistake there could still be two קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to אביי: Say that when he lies on purpose he is liable for one קרבן, but when he lies by mistake he is liable for two!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back on אביי's answer from step 16. They suggest the ״one קרבן only″ rule covers only a person who lied on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 we learned that שבועת העדות brings a קרבן even במזיד. A שבועת ביטוי only brings a קרבן בשוגג. So the רבנן suggest: במזיד only the שבועת העדות קרבן applies, which is one, but בשוגג both apply, which is two.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / maybe it means (a suggested alternative)
He is liable (obligated)
One
Two

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Abaye:
Say: on purpose, he is liable for one [offering];
by mistake, he is liable for two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the new חידוש from step 18 (a קרבן even במזיד) to bring back the two-קרבנות idea that אביי rejected in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim from step 16 that ״לְאַחַת״ rules out two קרבנות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ״one only″ rule could be limited to מזיד, which leaves room for two קרבנות בשוגג.

steps.title: אביי: the ״one only″ rule must be talking about a mistake
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא of ״לְאַחַת״ cannot be about מזיד, because then two was never possible. So it must teach one קרבן even בשוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Isn't this what they said: ״לְאַחַת״ means for one you make him liable, and you do not make him liable for two? And if it were on purpose, could there even be two?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his position. He shows that the ברייתא's limit only makes sense for a person who sinned by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק only needs to rule out two קרבנות in a case where two could have come up. במזיד, שבועת ביטוי brings no קרבן at all, so two was never possible there. So the ברייתא must be talking about שוגג, and even there he brings only one.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this exactly what they said? (pointing to a known source)
For one (from the פסוק ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״)
You make him liable
Is there even...? (a question expecting ″no″)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a false שבועת העדות brings only one קרבן, even בשוגג. The ״לְאַחַת״ limit only makes sense for a mistake.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Is this not what they said:
"For one" —
for one you make him liable,
and you do not make him liable for two;
and if it were on purpose,
is there even a case of two?
phrases.notes: On purpose, a שבועת ביטוי brings no קרבן at all. So a limit to ″one″ there would teach nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's suggestion from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא: it must be talking about שוגג, since only there could two have come up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ״one only″ rule might be about מזיד, which would leave two קרבנות בשוגג.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is about שוגג, so there is never more than one קרבן.

steps.title: רבא: a case taken out of a general rule follows only its new law
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason for one קרבן. שבועת העדות was part of the general rule of oaths and was taken out to teach a new law, so only that new law applies to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because it is a matter that was included in a general rule and was taken out to be judged with a new law, you have in it only its new law alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the רבנן's question in a different way. He does not need the פסוק ״לְאַחַת״ to rule out two קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבועת העדות was really part of the general category of שבועת ביטוי. The תורה took it out and gave it its own new rules, such as a קרבן even במזיד. By the rule of דבר שבכלל ויצא לידון בדבר החדש, it now follows only its own new rules. So the שבועת ביטוי קרבן no longer applies to it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that was included in a general rule
And was taken out to be judged with a new law
Its new law (what is new about it)
Only, alone

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the classic rules for reading the תורה (one of the י״ג מידות). Here it explains why a single act cannot bring two קרבנות.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Because it is a matter that was included in a general rule
and it was taken out to be judged with a new law —
phrases.notes: The general rule is שבועת ביטוי. The new law is the special rules of שבועת העדות.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ בּוֹ אֶלָּא חִידּוּשׁוֹ בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: you have in it only its new law alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה דָּבָר שֶׁבַּכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than אביי's (step 20) to the רבנן's question about two קרבנות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses a rule for reading the תורה instead of a word in a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבועת העדות might still count as a שבועת ביטוי too, and bring a second קרבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once it was taken out to get a new law, it follows only its own law, so there is one קרבן.

steps.title: Does אביי hold that the oath of ביטוי still exists here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference: since אביי needed a פסוק to stop two קרבנות, he must hold that the שבועת ביטוי still exists inside a שבועת העדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this it follows that אביי holds the oath still exists in the world?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices what follows from the gap between אביי and רבא, and asks about it. This line sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the שבועת ביטוי side disappears completely. אביי needed a פסוק to block a second קרבן. That suggests the שבועת ביטוי side is still there in his view, and only the קרבן is limited. The surprised tone shows the גמרא is about to look into this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: From this it follows (an inference)
It exists
In the world, meaning it still exists in principle

phrases.english: By inference, Abaye holds:
the oath still exists in the world?!
phrases.notes: He means the שבועת ביטוי side of the oath is still there, even though it brings no second קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares אביי's answer (step 20) with רבא's (step 21) and asks what אביי's answer shows about his view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to אביי, a שבועת ביטוי still exists inside a שבועת העדות, with only the extra קרבן blocked by the פסוק.

steps.title: אביי's own statement seems to contradict him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference from Step 22. אביי himself said that according to רב, 'I swear I know testimony for you' does not count as a שבועת ביטוי, because its negative version is a שבועת העדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't אביי say: רב agrees that if someone says to his friend 'I swear I know testimony for you,' and it turns out he did not know any, he is exempt, since the oath does not work in the form 'I do not know testimony for you'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what it just inferred about אביי by quoting a different statement of אביי that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a שבועת ביטוי needs to be an oath that could be said both ways, yes and no. אביי said the oath 'I know testimony for you' fails this test, because 'I do not know testimony for you' is a שבועת העדות and not a ביטוי. So אביי seems to hold that ביטוי does not exist inside an oath about testimony, which is the opposite of what Step 22 said.

keyTerms.meaning: רב agrees (even he admits this case)
and it turned out / it was found
exempt (here, from bringing a קרבן)
since it does not exist / does not work
an oath a person says on his own, about doing or not doing something, or about a fact

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two oaths. 'I know testimony for you' is the positive oath here. Its negative version, 'I do not know testimony for you,' is exactly a שבועת העדות, and that is why it cannot count as a ביטוי.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye say:
Rav agrees in a case where one says to his friend
"I swear that I know testimony for you,"
and it turned out that he did not know any for him
that he is exempt,
since it does not work
in the form "I do not know testimony for you"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of Step 22 by quoting a contradicting statement of אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that אביי holds a שבועת ביטוי still exists inside a שבועת העדות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי elsewhere ruled the oath 'I know testimony for you' is not a ביטוי because its negative is a שבועת העדות, which shows he holds ביטוי does not exist inside עדות.

steps.title: אביי changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אביי took back his earlier statement about רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי took back that statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction simply: אביי retracted the earlier statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once אביי took back what he said about 'I know testimony for you,' there is no contradiction left. The inference of Step 22 stands: אביי holds that a שבועת ביטוי still exists inside a שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: he went back on it / he changed his mind
from that (earlier statement)

phrases.english: Abaye retracted that statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the two contradicting statements was withdrawn by its author.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements of אביי stand, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי withdrew his statement about רב's case, so his view that ביטוי exists inside עדות stands.

steps.title: Opening a second answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a second, different way to answer the contradiction. The answer itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is about to give a second answer to the contradiction, and that answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula ואיבעית אימא tells us the first answer (אביי changed his mind) is not the only option. The coming answer will try to keep both statements of אביי without saying he retracted.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say instead:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces an alternative answer to the קשיא of Step 23, alongside the answer in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer (introduction only; the content follows).
